I know this game has gotten a lot of hate for a lot of valid reasons. But I’m playing Fallout in space and I’m loving it.

The gameplay is extremely satisfying for me and I actually have this yearning to go out and explore space. The fact that there are so many planets with resources and missions and storylines really feels alive to me. I’m actually happy I had low expectations for this game, because I’m having an awesome time and I’d even go so far to say that I’m proud of Bethesda for the care they put into this game. Not proud of Bethesda for the paid mods, but just about everything else feels really good to me. I know people talk about wanting to actually fly the ships on-planet and leave atmosphere and such. That would be cool, but I didn’t expect that. I expected fast travel, and I still feel immersed in the space captain experience. Character customization was also really good in my opinion.

My character’s name is Eugene Starfield and he is the Dragonborn of space.

After 300 hours in game, I've decided to go with the feedback.

Firstly, no, this game isn't even close to Skyrim or Fallout 3, Fallout : New Vegas or even to Fallout 4.

It's a mediocre game at best, which you rate for 6/10.

Potential is good, but it still needs lots of updates to be a good game. Starfield has to beat repetitiveness and disconnection of world.

What made Bethesda games best were exploration and the connection of world. Yes, we have 1000 planets, but there are no stories or anything there which you can explore. Even the settled planets where you face major cities/settlements lack stories and exploration potential.

Basically the game has zero exploration, because everything outside of cities are procedurally generated and everything is the same with no stories in them, no interesting locations or creatures , just sometimes differently colored themed planets.

The game isn't bad, it's an OK game. However, it lacks everything Bethesda stands for ( the exploration and stories with in).

Leading up to this game releasing I was excited. I want to enjoy this game. The game is full of elements that I do enjoy. Space Exploration, ship and outpost building. The game launched with no shortage of bugs. One of the first things Bethesda 'fixed' was the ship service merchant chest in New Atlantis. Probably wouldnt be an issue if a similar bug didnt still exist in Skyrim to this day. More recently, Bethesda 'fixed' the player ability to reroll stats on the Mantis suit. Both of these bugs are generally harmless in a single player game. Meanwhile, theres still a bug in the game that causes Temples to not spawn. This is a core mechanic of the game that still hasnt been fixed and can be considered game-breaking. The list goes on and on. The game feels like a lot of potential and broken promises. Despite buying it on sale, I kinda feel like I want to return the game and get a refund. Ps. Lets not overlook the paid mods! Basically anything is permissible IF you pay for it, achievements arent disabled. IF you run a free mod that does the same thing the achievements are disabled. I really want to like and enjoy this game but get the impression that Bethesda doesnt want people to like or enjoy it considering the 'fixes' theyve implemented while ignoring the bugs that need fixing.

I was gifted Starfield when it came out, but with all the negative reviews I put off playing it for a long time because of that.

So coming into the game with low expectations I was genuinely surprised at how good the game is!

The characters are interesting, even some random sidequest NPCs who aren't going to matter in the long run are interesting and the voice acting is well done. Which is impressive for random sidequest characters.

The combat is good, a little chaotic, but honestly more exciting than Fallout 4.

The space combat is my favorite, the only problem is that I wish there was more of it. It took me a bit to get used to at first, I struggled with fighting large groups of enemies, but I played the simulator in MAST 5 times through and it worked as a good place to learn how to win combat.

Starfield isn't the best game I've ever played, there are some flaws, but it's honestly one of the better single player titles that have come out the last couple years.

The core issue with Starfield is that it's fundamentally broken, and no amount of patches will be able to 'fix' this game.

The game's biggest flaw is its fast-travel system. Players can teleport from any point on the map, leading to an overreliance on fast travel. As a result, much of the gameplay is spent staring at loading screens and repetitive animations, which detracts significantly from the overall experience.

What the developers should have done is implement a system similar to Skyrim, where players are forced to manually trek from one location to another until they reach a fast-travel point. This mechanic has been successful in nearly every adventure and RPG game for the past 30 years, so it's puzzling why they deviated from it.

Starfield would have had much more depth if it had been limited to, say, 2-3 Skyrim-sized hand-crafted planets.

Even since I started playing Skyrim in 2011, and later going back to play earlier Bethesda titles, I have been a fan of their gameworld and creation. I never really play these games for the mechanics. I play games for the deep lore behind them, the stories I can tell to myself with my characters, and just the exploration.

With that said, Starfield had the potential to be one of the few sci-fi games I would enjoy, sadly thats not the case. This game is boring. It looks good, may even be one of Bethesda's most "polished" game ever, but it doesn't mean it is a good game or entertaining game. This game lacks the charm of their past games, most of it I contribute to lack of creative quest design and writing, lack of exploration, and the game feel half finished in places.

We could speculate that Bethesda has launched this game "unfinished" for modders to finish for them, but I'm not the person for that convo.

Most of what I have said here, is probably something thats been said by multiple people before me with much more experience reviewing games and knowledge regarding game design.

In my personal opinion, it is not worth buying. This game is boring, and lacks charm. It may not be for me, but you (the person reading this) may not feel the same.

I simply cannot stomach the loading screens after loading screens after loading screens. Lack of any ground vehicles. Lack of actual space exploration. Tried to let go of those hopes and focus on the story, but the story is uninteresting. Just fetch quest after fetch quest going back to the lodge. Faction quests that have ZERO consequences depending on who you side with. Once it sets in just how shallow and repetitive the game is, you realize there is no excitement left to be had. Just loading screens and mediocrity. I wish I spent that $70 on Cyberpunk instead.
